newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea declares mourning over for late Kim.
newsitem.headline: North Korea declares mourning over for late Kim.

text.p: North Korea declared on Tuesday that the three-year mourning period for its late president Kim Il-sung was over, opening the way for his son to take over the two key offices of party chief and state president.

But North Korea's state-run media, reporting addresses at Tuesday's national memorial service in Pyongyang on the third anniversary of Kim's death, did not use either of the titles in referring to his son and successor Kim Jong-il.

"We solemnly re-state our heartful pledge to our father the great leader (Kim Il-sung) at this important occasion when the mourning is over," said Foreign Minister and Vice Premier Kim Yong-nam, according to the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) monitored in Tokyo.
Kim Jong-il was present at the memorial service held at Pyongyang's Kumsusan Memorial Palace but did not make a speech.

Kim Jong-il, although in undisputed control of the country and commander-in-chief of the military, has yet to be named general-secretary of the ruling Korean Workers' (communist) Party or state president.

North Korea watchers in Seoul and Tokyo said Kim Jong-il may take up the two posts sometime later this year because to assume them swiftly after the end of the mourning period would be considered insensitive to the memory of the elder Kim, who was the founding father of the nation.
In his address, Foreign Minister Kim said there was no question over the succession itself but used only the "great leader" title when referring to Kim Jong-il.
"Long ago he most brilliantly solved the question of inheritance of the leadership in Korea with a high sense of responsibility for socialism and the future of the people," Kim Yong-nam said.
"Today the Korean revolution goes on along the straight road...under the guidance of the great leader comrade Kim Jong-il, the most faithful heir to the cause of comrade Kim Il-sung," he said.
KCNA used Kim junior's formal military titles in references to him.

"The great leader comrade Kim Jong-il, chairman of the National Defence Commission of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and supreme commander of the Korean People's Army, attended the meeting together with senior party and state officials," the news agency said.
KCNA said representatives of the army, ruling party and national youth league made addresses praising Kim Il-sung's deeds and pledging loyalty to Kim Jong-il.

"The officers and men of the People's Army will remain loyal to the supreme commander with unshakable faith and pure conscience and defend the headquarters of the revolution headed by comrade Kim Jong-il...by giving full play to the spirit of defending the leader with lives, the spirit of human bombs and the spirit of suicidal attack," Vice-Marshal Jo Myong-rok said on behalf of the military.

"All the Youth League officials and young people, true to their pledge made in tears of blood before the bier of the president, will become young guards and death-defying corps to defend comrade Kim Jong-il with their lives," said Choe Ryong-hae, first secretary of the central committee of the Kim Il-sung Socialist Youth League.

KCNA said the thousands of people who attended the service in the plaza next to the palace observed a moment's silence for the late Kim. Guns were fired to honour the memory of the late president after the meeting, it said.
